title: Sysprose verify report
description: What `npm run sysprose -- verify <file> --json` emits on stdout. The top-level `verdict` block is the exit-code arithmetic and is the ONLY thing an automation needs to read: `verdict.exitCode` is what the process exited with, including the degraded-model rule that lowers a clean sweep to 2. Read docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md's `verify` section for the contract in words — its 1 means REFUTED, which is not what the reporting subcommands' 1 means.

ok.description: Did the file load cleanly? False ⇒ `verdict.exitCode` is 2.

degraded.description: Present only when the model did not load cleanly. A verdict over half a model is not a verdict, so its presence forces exit 2.

discharged.description: Obligations discharged non-vacuously BY THE ENGINE THAT WAS ASKED FOR. Under `--engine literal` a `holds-at-values` row counts; under `smt` and `auto` it does not.

violated.description: Refuted with every feature at its model value. Nothing else is exit 1.

inconclusive.description: Everything undecided, vacuous and tool-absent included. Any un-forgiven one is exit 2.

designAdmitted.description: Refutations obtained under `--free`: a design the model admits, exit 2, never 1.

engine.description: What `auto` resolved to. It resolves to `smt` or reports `verification/tool-absent`; it NEVER falls back to `literal`.

forgiven.description: How many inconclusive rows `--allow-inconclusive` lowered. It lowers `verification/timeout` and `verification/unsupported-construct` and nothing else.

exitCode.description: From the obligations alone. The top-level `verdict.exitCode` is this one with the degraded-model rule applied, and it is the one the process exits with.

premises.description: The assumptions, evaluated BEFORE the guarantee. A pass that stands on three assumptions is a different claim from an unconditional one.
